title: Executive Brief
body:
How to use this plan
This document is the operating blueprint for HighLife from August 2026 through the end of 2027. It is designed to 
answer five questions every week: What are we trying to build? What number are we chasing? What work matters 
now? Who owns it? What tells us whether it is working?
The plan in one page
Decision HighLife operating answer
North Star
Build a globally relevant creative company under one 
umbrella: Music, Media and Merch, with events and 
community as connective tissue.
2027 financial goal $250K cumulative revenue from Aug. 10, 2026 through Dec. 
31, 2027. Operate toward a $20K-$25K monthly exit run-rate.
Primary growth bet Podcast production and recurring media services. Treat 
podcasting as the cash engine inside the Media pillar.
Current baseline ~$9K/month: roughly $8K music studio and $1K podcast.
Resource allocation Approximately 65% podcast/revenue growth, 15% music, 
10% HighLife media brand, 10% merch/events experiments.
Leadership cadence Monday 10:00 AM business meeting; Wednesday 5:30 PM 
team meeting; Sunday 4:00 PM brand meeting.
Content cadence
HL Podcast weekly; podcast commercials 2x/month; HL 
Freestyle 1x/month on Saturday; one event/month, eventually 
two.
Systems HighLevel owns leads and customers. HighLife Roadmap 
owns execution, OKRs, owners, deadlines and SOPs.
Document map
STRATEGY
• North Star and five-year vision
• Current-state diagnosis
• Revenue path and portfolio logic
• Podcast offer and ICP
• Growth funnel and sales system
OPERATIONS
• Weekly and monthly cadence
• Quarterly OKRs
• KPI scorecard
• Team and hiring triggers
• Roadmap, SOPs and 90-day execution plan
The core management rule
Do not make every HighLife pillar equal priority every week. Keep all three alive, but concentrate growth 
resources on the one engine with the highest revenue ceiling: podcasting.

title: North Star
body:
The five-year vision
HighLife is not trying to remain only a recording studio. The five-year ambition is a globally relevant creative 
company with dominance across three connected pillars: Music, Media and Merch. Events and community are the 
distribution layer that make the three pillars feel like one culture instead of separate businesses.
5-YEAR NORTH STAR
Global cultural relevance through Music + Media + Merch, built under one HighLife umbrella.
What each pillar is responsible for
Pillar Role in the ecosystem Near-term job
MUSIC Cultural engine
Protect the existing studio base, technical 
reputation, engineers, artist community 
and creative credibility.
MEDIA Cash + audience engine
Scale podcast production first; use owned 
HighLife content to grow authority and 
distribution.
MERCH Commerce + identity engine
Build slowly through limited drops, 
collaborations and event-linked validation 
instead of inventory-heavy bets.
EVENTS Community connector
Create revenue, leads, content and 
community moments that feed all three 
pillars.
Values that should survive the scale
HighLife already publicly defines four values: Artist First, Fearless Creativity, Respect & Integrity, and Adapt & 
Innovate. The growth plan should strengthen those values, not replace them with a generic corporate culture.
WHAT HIGH LIFE SHOULD BECOME
• The DMV creative home for serious artists and media 
creators
• A full-service media partner for established professionals 
and brands
• An owned media platform with recognizable shows and 
formats
• A consumer-facing brand whose merch and events mean 
something
WHAT HIGH LIFE SHOULD NOT BECOME
• A cheap room-rental marketplace
• A content agency that says yes to every project
• A meeting-heavy company with no scoreboard
• A business that burns cash chasing every creative idea at 
once
Source note: HighLife public story, values and community pages reviewed August 10, 2026.

body:

What is already working
 Established HighLife brand, physical studios, technical team, interns and engineers already in place.
 Podcast suite has one room with 3-4 set configurations, multi-camera equipment, microphones, lighting and 
production staff.
 Public pricing is premium enough to support a high-value model: video podcast production starts at $300/hour 
while music sessions are typically around $60-$75/hour depending on location.
 HighLife already offers the full post-production stack: video editing, audio editing, short-form clips, 
mixing/mastering and on-location recording.
 New marketing/sales partner operates ads, AI outbound, CRM automation and HighLevel; compensation is 15% 
of the first collected sale.
 Initial demand signal is promising: 10 podcast tours booked in one recent week, the strongest tour volume to 
date.
The diagnosis
Constraint Reality Management response
Music capacity Current hourly music model likely tops out 
around $10K-$12K/month.
Protect it; do not expect it to carry the 
growth target.
Podcast capacity Only one room, but it is currently far from a 
near-term revenue bottleneck. Fill the room before discussing expansion.
Sales Historically barren; now the new marketing 
engine is generating tours.
Shift attention from lead generation alone 
to conversion, recurring packages and 
retention.
Leadership Jaco + JoJo are the only high-level 
business leaders today.
Keep decision-making tight; add 
fractional/contract leverage by trigger, not 
titles.
Execution Many creative priorities can compete for 
attention.
Use one weekly cadence, three quarterly 
OKRs and the Roadmap as the source of 
truth.
Key conclusion
The 2026-2027 problem is not "we need more services." HighLife already has the service stack. The problem is 
turning demand into a repeatable sales-to-recurring-revenue machine.

base plan below reaches exactly $250K. HighLife should still manage internally toward a stretch result so one

The operating flywheel
Step What happens

title: Podcast Revenue Engine
body:
Sell the show, not the room hour
HighLife can continue advertising a $300/hour video podcast session, but the internal sales goal should be 
recurring full-service relationships. Established clients are not buying cameras and microphones; they are buying 
a professional media presence without having to build and manage a production team.
Current public service stack
Service Current public pricing snapshot Strategic role
Video podcast production Starting at $300/hour Premium capture product and top-of-
funnel anchor.
Audio podcast production Starting at $100/hour Lower-complexity option; not the main 
growth engine.
Video editing Up to 60 min: $350; 60-90 min: $450 Highest-value post-production upsell and 
recurring deliverable.
Audio editing Up to 60 min: $200 Useful for audio distribution and polished 
deliverables.
Mixing & mastering Up to 2 hours: $200 Quality and consistency upsell.
Short-form clips 3 clips: $150 Growth deliverable; easy recurring bundle 
component.
On-location recording Custom quote High-value corporate, event and executive 
opportunity.
Pricing source: HighLife public podcast page reviewed August 10, 2026. The pricing calculator is a dynamic quote 
tool and should remain the operational quote surface while package architecture is refined.
Why podcast economics deserve disproportionate focus
4.3x
ROOM-HOUR PRICE
~$300 podcast vs. ~$70 music
$800
ILLUSTRATIVE EPISODE
1 hr + edit + 3 clips
$3.2K
ILLUSTRATIVE WEEKLY CLIENT
4 full-service episodes/month
Illustrative math: one 1-hour video episode at $300 + a <=60-minute video edit at $350 + three short clips at $150 
= $800 gross revenue before optional audio work or other add-ons. Four episodes per month = $3,200. This is 
revenue math, not profit math; editor labor and production costs must be tracked.

Recommended recurring package architecture
Offer Recommended price Designed for Core scope
Studio Session $300/hr One-off or trial clients
Video capture with HighLife 
production team; raw files; upsell 
post-production.
Biweekly Authority $1,750/mo Established professionals starting 
a serious show
2 x 1-hour video sessions, 2 full 
edits, 6 short clips total, reserved 
scheduling, standard delivery.
Weekly Authority $3,250/mo Active brands and creators
4 x 1-hour sessions, 4 full edits, 
12 short clips, audio polish, 
priority scheduling.
Executive Media Engine $5,000+/mo HNW, political, medical, corporate 
or media clients
Weekly production plus 
expanded clip volume, strategy, 
distribution support, custom 
graphics and/or on-location 
options.
Package rule
Do not finalize pricing until HighLife measures real editor hours, production labor, revisions, sales commission 
and payment fees. Bundle convenience, priority and output - not deep discounts. Use 3-month commitments and 
autopay for recurring packages.
Upsells that increase account value
 Additional short-form clips and clip packs.
 Thumbnail and graphic package.
 Audio-only distribution master and platform-ready exports.
 Extra cameras, guests, hours or extended edit length.
 On-location executive, corporate, conference and event recording.
 Commercial or branded content production around the podcast.
 Publishing/distribution support where HighLife has operational capacity.
 Sponsor-message insertion and branded integrations.
Recurring client retention system
Moment Standard
At close Autopay, term, scope, reserved cadence and deliverable 
expectations are explicit.
Kickoff One-page show brief: audience, purpose, visual set, cadence, 
deliverables, approval path.
Every session Producer checks next episode date before client leaves.
Delivery Send assets + next-action note; capture revision reasons to 
improve process.
Monthly For package clients, review output, upcoming topics and any 
additional content needs.
After 3 wins Ask for testimonial, referral and/or introduction to another 
qualified brand.

title: Ideal Customer + Positioning
body:
Broad verticals, narrow buying signals
HighLife can serve multiple verticals without marketing to "everyone." The common thread is an established 
person or organization with a reason to publish consistently, enough budget to value quality, and a desire to avoid 
building an internal production team.
Primary ICP clusters
Cluster Why they buy Best message
Business owners / executives Authority, lead generation, recruiting, 
thought leadership
"Turn your expertise into a professional 
media presence without building a media 
department."
Medical / healthcare leaders Education, credibility, patient/community 
communication
"Studio-grade production with a team that 
handles the technical complexity."
Politics / policy / associations Ideas, constituency, advocacy, visibility "Reliable, professional multi-camera 
production in the DC market."
Established podcasters with weak quality Upgrade visual/audio brand without losing 
format
"Keep your show. Upgrade how the world 
experiences it."
Media personalities / HNW creators Consistency, brand polish, convenience "Show up, record, leave with a production 
engine behind you."
Qualification signals
GREEN FLAGS
• Clear reason for the show beyond "I want a podcast"
• Plans to publish at least 2x/month
• Existing business, audience, brand or professional 
reputation
• Values convenience and production quality
• Decision-maker attends the tour
• Can commit to a 3-month content cadence
RED FLAGS
• Pure price shopping
• No publishing plan or topic ownership
• One-off project with no strategic value unless highly 
profitable
• Expects unlimited edits or undefined deliverables
• No decision authority or budget clarity
• Wants HighLife to invent the entire business/brand before 
agreeing to scope
Core positioning
HighLife is the DMV production partner for serious voices: professional video, audio, editing and content support 
under one roof.
Tour discovery questions
1. Why are you starting or upgrading the show now?
2. Who is the audience and what should the show do for your business or brand?
3. How often do you want to publish?
4. What is hardest about your current process: recording, editing, clips, consistency, distribution or all of it?
5. Who is involved in approving content and budget?
6. What would a great 90 days of content look like?
7. Would you rather manage vendors every episode or have one team own the production system?

body:
Make the 10-tour week repeatable
The recent 10-tour week is a real signal, but the new scoreboard is not "leads." It is the entire conversion chain: 
qualified lead -> showed tour -> paid first sale -> recurring package -> retained client.

Two commercial shoots per month - what to create
Creative type Example angle CTA
Proof / testimonial Show a real client transformation, set, final 
clip or quote Book a tour

Each commercial shoot should create multiple hooks and edits rather than one final ad. The marketing team can 
test persona x hook x offer combinations without requiring new production every week.
Sales compensation rule
Keep the 15% first-sale commission for now
Pay commission on collected net service revenue after payment clears, not on uncollected quotes. Review the 
structure after 60-90 days of data. If recurring packages become the priority, consider a small one-time bonus 
for closing 3-month package commitments rather than paying lifetime residuals.

title: Capacity + Service Operations
body:
One podcast room is enough - for now
HighLife has one podcast room and can shoot only one podcast at a time, but that is not currently the limiting 
factor. At $300/hour, even 10 paid podcast recording hours per week equates to roughly $13K/month of recording 
revenue before any edits or clips. The near-term challenge is sales, scheduling, post-production and retention - 
not a second room.
10 HRS/WK
PODCAST ROOM USE
~$12.9K/mo recording revenue
15 HRS/WK
PODCAST ROOM USE
~$19.4K/mo recording revenue
1 ROOM
CURRENT CAPACITY
Expand only after threshold is proven
Capacity triggers
Signal Trigger Action
Prime-time room utilization >60% for 8 consecutive weeks Raise/segment pricing, expand hours, 
tighten recurring reserved slots.
Prime-time room utilization >75% for 8 weeks + meaningful waitlist Begin second-room / alternate-space 
business case.
Editing backlog Typical delivery repeatedly exceeds 7 
business days
Add contract editor capacity before adding 
more marketing volume.
Revisions >20%-25% of jobs require avoidable 
rework
Fix pre-production brief, templates and 
approval process.
Founder sales load Jaco spends >5 hours/week on routine 
follow-up for 4+ weeks Add dedicated closer/pipeline coordinator.
Client success load 8-10+ recurring clients and missed follow-
ups appear
Assign a podcast producer/client success 
owner.
Service standards
 Every recurring show has a one-page production brief and reserved recording cadence.
 Session starts on time; set, cameras, lighting, audio and files are checked before client arrival.
 File naming, storage and handoff follow the same convention every time.
 Post-production scope is explicit before the edit begins.
 One standard revision round unless package says otherwise; extra revisions are billable.
 Typical editing delivery remains within the public 5-7 business-day expectation or client is proactively notified.
 Every finished project becomes an opportunity for testimonial, referral, upsell or case study.

Sunday rule
Batch the content, not the meetings. Shoot the weekly HL Podcast and scheduled commercials on Sunday, then 
use the 4:00 PM Brand Meeting to decide what the brand does next - not to recap business metrics that belong 
on Monday.
Weekly commitment rule
 Every Monday, each leadership owner leaves with no more than 3-5 critical commitments for the week.
 Every commitment has one owner and one due date in the Roadmap.
 If a task has no owner, it is not a task; it is an idea.
 Status updates should be visible in the Roadmap. Meeting time is for decisions, blockers and accountability.
 Any initiative that does not support a quarterly OKR goes to Backlog unless it is an operational emergency.

title: Meeting Playbooks
body:
Three meetings, three different jobs
Monday 10:00 AM - Business / Leadership (60-75 min)
Block Time Agenda
1. Scoreboard 10 min
Cash collected vs target; podcast 
revenue/MRR; music revenue; bookings; 
major wins/misses.
2. Sales funnel 15 min
Leads, tours booked/showed, proposals, 
close rate, stuck deals, follow-up, 
marketing report.
3. Operations 10 min
Upcoming bookings, delivery backlog, 
client issues, engineer/room capacity, 
quality.
4. People 5 min Intern/team progress, staffing needs, 
accountability concerns.
5. Money 10 min Spend, ad budget, commissions, 
collections, unusual expense, cash needs.
6. Roadmap + SOP 10 min Quarter OKRs, blocked tasks, SOP 
progress, decisions needed.
7. Commit 10 min Owner + due date for the 3-5 most 
important commitments each.
This agenda incorporates the whiteboard list: ops, recap, upcoming tasks, bookings, revenue vs. target, Roadmap 
check, intern/team progress, media check, marketing check-in, budget/spend and SOPs - but orders them around 
the scoreboard first.
Wednesday 5:30 PM - Team (45-60 min)
 Wins and recognition - 5 min.
 This week / next week bookings and event needs - 10 min.
 Client-service or technical issues that everyone can learn from - 10 min.
 Training topic / SOP of the week - 15 min.
 Intern assignments, engineer accountability and team responsibilities - 10 min.
 Announcements, culture and questions - 5 min.
Sunday 4:00 PM - Brand (45-60 min)
 Rank Music, Media and Merch 1-3 for the coming week based on the quarter plan.
 Review what is being published from the content bank.
 Decide the next HL Podcast, freestyle, commercial or campaign creative priorities.
 Review upcoming monthly event and the primary business objective.
 Make creative decisions; assign owners; stop before it becomes a second Monday business meeting.
Meeting hygiene
No meeting should exist just to say what happened. Use the Roadmap and HighLevel for status. Meetings exist to 
interpret numbers, solve blockers, make decisions and assign commitments.

title: Monthly Management
body:
Turn the first Monday into the monthly review
The first Monday business meeting of each month becomes a 90-minute Monthly Business Review. It replaces a 
separate extra meeting; the weekly rhythm stays intact.

Financial discipline: Build a separate P&L view by business line. The company cannot know what to scale until it 
knows contribution margin by music, podcast, event and merch. Revenue alone is not enough.

title: Quarterly Okrs
body:
Three company objectives per quarter. No more.
HighLife should run quarterly planning with a maximum of three company objectives. Pillar work supports the 
company objectives rather than creating twenty competing OKRs. The Roadmap should tag every meaningful 
project to one of the three.
OKR architecture
Objective Always answers Typical KRs
O1 - Revenue engine How are we growing durable revenue? Revenue, podcast MRR, recurring clients, 
close rate, channel economics
O2 - Operating system Can the team deliver the growth reliably? Turnaround, SOPs, Roadmap use, 
utilization, retention, staffing
O3 - Brand / cultural footprint Are Music, Media and Merch getting 
stronger without derailing O1?
HL Podcast, freestyles, events, proof 
content, partnerships, merch tests
OKR scoring
At quarter-end, score each KR 0.0-1.0. A quarter is not a failure because every KR was not 1.0. The purpose is to 
force prioritization and learn what moved the business.

title: Quarter-By-Quarter Plan
body:
Launch Sprint: Aug. 10 - Sep. 30, 2026
O1 - Prove the podcast acquisition-to-recurring funnel
 KR1: Book at least 50 podcast tours during the sprint.
 KR2: Achieve at least 65% tour show rate and 25% tour-to-first-sale close rate.
 KR3: Close at least 10 new paid podcast customers.
 KR4: Exit September with at least $2.5K in podcast MRR or equivalent contracted monthly recurring value.
 KR5: Every lead and opportunity lives in HighLevel with stage, owner, source and next action.
O2 - Install the HighLife operating system
 KR1: Hold >=90% of scheduled Monday, Wednesday and Sunday meetings.
 KR2: Move all leadership commitments into the Roadmap with owner, due date and OKR tag.
 KR3: Publish the first 7 core SOPs: lead response, tour, proposal/follow-up, client onboarding, podcast session, 
file handoff/editing, revision/delivery.
O3 - Restart brand cadence without losing revenue focus
 KR1: Publish/record the HL Podcast weekly for the remainder of the sprint.
 KR2: Complete at least 3 podcast commercial creative batches during the partial two-month sprint.
 KR3: Run 2 HL Freestyle activations and 2 monthly events or documented equivalent if calendar constraints 
require one event to shift.
Sprint revenue checkpoint
$16K cumulative target from Aug. 10 through Sep. 30. The point of this sprint is not maximum scale; it is proving 
the system before Q4.

Q4 2026 - Convert momentum into a real business 
engine
O1 - Reach $36K quarter revenue and make podcasting material
 KR1: Collect $36K total revenue across October-December.
 KR2: Exit December at approximately $13K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Reach at least $4K-$4.5K monthly podcast revenue and $4K podcast MRR or close equivalent.
 KR4: Sustain >=70% tour show rate and >=25%-30% tour-to-first-sale close rate.
 KR5: Reach >=35% first-sale-to-recurring conversion for qualified podcast clients.
O2 - Make delivery reliable enough to scale
 KR1: 90%+ of standard post-production delivered within the published 5-7 business-day expectation.
 KR2: Implement standardized briefs, file naming, edit templates and revision tracking.
 KR3: Complete a service cost study for every podcast package before expanding paid spend materially.
O3 - Build visible consistency
 KR1: 12-13 HL Podcast episodes in Q4.
 KR2: 6 podcast commercial batches, 3 HL Freestyles and 3 events.
 KR3: Capture at least 6 usable client testimonials/case-study assets.
EOY 2026 decision gate: Rockville
Question Data required
Keep, renew, expand, buy or exit? Trailing 3-month location revenue and contribution margin
Is Rockville strategically essential? Unique clients, utilization, overflow value, geographic reach
Is the capital better used elsewhere? Lease obligations, buildout needs, podcast/media growth 
opportunities
What is the 12-month forecast? Bookings, music ceiling, potential alternative use of space

Q1 2027 - Retention and recurring revenue
O1 - Collect $43K and deepen recurring podcast revenue
 KR1: Collect $43K total revenue in Q1.
 KR2: Exit March at $15K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Reach $5K-$6K podcast MRR / contracted recurring value.
 KR4: Maintain at least 6 active recurring podcast accounts or equivalent revenue concentration.
O2 - Make client retention a system
 KR1: Measure 30-, 60- and 90-day recurring retention; target >=80% 90-day retention after sample size is 
meaningful.
 KR2: Install monthly client check-ins for higher-tier recurring accounts.
 KR3: Reduce avoidable revision and missed-deadline causes month over month.
O3 - Turn HighLife content into authority
 KR1: 13 HL Podcast episodes, 6 podcast commercial batches, 3 freestyles and 3 events.
 KR2: Build a reusable proof library: client clips, testimonials, behind-the-scenes and final outputs tagged by 
ICP.

Q2 2027 - Diversify acquisition and add operational 
leverage
O1 - Collect $47K and reach $6K-$7K+ podcast monthly revenue
 KR1: Collect $47K in Q2.
 KR2: Exit June at $16K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Build at least 8 active recurring podcast clients or equivalent recurring revenue book.
 KR4: At least 30% of new podcast revenue comes from referrals, organic, partnerships or events rather than 
paid acquisition alone.
O2 - Add leverage where workload proves the need
 KR1: Assign or hire a dedicated podcast client-success/producer owner if the trigger is reached.
 KR2: Establish an editor bench with backup capacity and consistent templates.
 KR3: Have monthly financial reporting with revenue and direct cost by business line.
O3 - Strengthen HighLife as an ecosystem
 KR1: Maintain owned-content and event cadence without missing revenue service standards.
 KR2: Run at least one merch preorder/collaboration test tied to a proven community moment rather than 
speculative inventory.

Q3 2027 - Scale what has proven itself
O1 - Collect $52K and push podcast toward $8K-$9K/month
 KR1: Collect $52K in Q3.
 KR2: Exit September at $18K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Reach $8K-$9K monthly podcast/media revenue with at least 50% coming from recurring clients.
 KR4: Increase average podcast account value through packages and upsells without increasing avoidable 
churn.
O2 - Make a data-based capacity decision
 KR1: Track sellable podcast hours, prime-time utilization, edit load and lead-to-booking wait time every month.
 KR2: Only build a second podcast room/business case if utilization and waitlist thresholds have been sustained.
 KR3: Ensure no single recurring client represents a dangerous percentage of podcast revenue.
O3 - Expand brand partnerships
 KR1: Build 3-5 active referral/brand/community partnerships that create measurable leads or content 
opportunities.
 KR2: Continue 1 event/month; test 2/month only if team capacity and event scorecards justify it.

Q4 2027 - Finish the goal and prepare the next era
O1 - Finish $250K cumulative and exit with a stronger run-rate
 KR1: Collect $56K in Q4 and finish at least $250K cumulative since Aug. 10, 2026.
 KR2: Exit December at $19K base monthly revenue; stretch toward $20K-$25K.
 KR3: Reach $9K-$12K+ monthly podcast/media revenue with at least 60% recurring where feasible.
 KR4: Finish 2027 with a clear 2028 budget, revenue target and reinvestment plan.
O2 - Make the company less founder-dependent
 KR1: Core sales, client-success, studio and delivery SOPs work without Jaco or JoJo manually touching every 
step.
 KR2: Role scorecards exist for every recurring contractor/leader.
 KR3: Bookkeeping/CPA reporting cadence and cash reserve policy are active.
O3 - Decide where the cash engine invests next
 KR1: Choose 2028 priority investments across owned media, music projects, merch, events and physical 
capacity based on 2027 returns.
 KR2: Publish a new three-year roadmap that converts the five-year cultural vision into specific bets.

title: Weekly Scoreboard
body:
Measure a small set of numbers relentlessly
Category Weekly metric Definition / use
REVENUE Cash collected Primary scoreboard against monthly target.
REVENUE Podcast revenue Recording + post + package revenue 
collected.
REVENUE Podcast MRR Contracted monthly recurring value on active 
recurring accounts.
REVENUE Music revenue Protect the existing studio base and detect 
declines early.
SALES Leads by source Paid, outbound, referral, organic, event.
SALES Tours booked / showed Measures calendar volume and show rate.
SALES Tour-to-first-sale close Shows whether tour and offer work.
SALES First-sale-to-recurring Shows whether the business is becoming 
durable.
MARKETING Spend / CPL / CAC Controls growth economics by channel.
OPS Podcast room hours Measures actual utilization, not anecdotes.
OPS Turnaround time Average and % inside service standard.
OPS Revision rate Flags bad briefs, editing quality or scope 
creep.
BRAND Cadence completed HL Podcast / commercial / freestyle / event.
PEOPLE Roadmap commitments completed Accountability without adding more meetings.
Monday scoreboard thresholds
Metric Green Yellow Red
Revenue vs monthly pace >=100% pace 90%-99% <90%
Tour show rate >=70% 60%-69% <60%
Tour close rate >=30% 20%-29% <20%
Recurring conversion >=40% 25%-39% <25%
Standard edit turnaround <=5-7 days 8-9 days 10+ days
Roadmap commitments >=85% on time 70%-84% <70%
Thresholds should be recalibrated after 60-90 days of real data. The important part is consistency: HighLife 
should use the same definitions every week so trends mean something.

title: Team + Leadership Design
body:
Grow leverage before hierarchy
Current operating structure
Role Primary ownership

Strategy, revenue target, key sales/partnerships, marketing

JoJo - Founder / President / Lead Engineer

Paid ads, AI outbound, HighLevel, landing pages/automation, 
pipeline generation, follow-up and sales conversion; 15% first-
sale commission.
Engineers / Producers Client experience, technical execution, on-time sessions, quality, 
upsell signals, retention.
Intern Team Research, outreach support, content/admin tasks, event support 
and project execution under clear owners.
Hiring / contractor triggers
Need Trigger Preferred structure first
Bookkeeping / CPA Immediately or as soon as monthly reporting 
is inconsistent
Fractional bookkeeper + CPA/tax advisor; do 
not wait for a full-time finance hire.
Pipeline coordinator / closer Tour volume stays high and routine follow-up 
consumes founder time
Commission / part-time contractor with clear 
CRM scorecard.
Podcast producer / client success 8-10+ recurring accounts or follow-ups begin 
slipping
Part-time / contractor, then full-time when 
economics support it.
Editor bench Delivery pushes beyond 7 business days or 
one editor becomes a bottleneck
Contract bench with standardized templates 
and QA.
Operations manager Revenue >$20K/month for several months 
and founders are still the routing layer
Hire only after SOPs exist so the role 
manages a system, not chaos.
Equity and board guidance
Do not give away ownership to solve a staffing problem
Use cash, commission and contractor structures for normal work. Consider equity only for a long-term executive-
level operator who materially changes company value, with vesting, a cliff, role/KPI expectations and legal 
counsel. If HighLife wants outside wisdom now, form an informal advisory circle rather than a formal board with 
governance power.
A useful advisory circle could include entertainment/media, finance/CPA, legal, sales/brand and DMV 
business/community expertise. Meet quarterly or semi-annually and bring them specific decisions, not routine 
updates.

title: Roadmap App + Execution System
body:
HighLevel tracks customers. Roadmap tracks the 
company.
The HighLife Roadmap should be the living operating layer for priorities, OKRs and commitments. It should not 
become a second CRM and should not duplicate every lead or booking already in HighLevel.
Every Roadmap item should contain
Field Purpose
Task / project Clear verb + outcome, not vague topic.
Owner Exactly one accountable person.
Pillar Revenue/Podcast, Music, Media, Merch, Events, Operations or 
Finance.
Quarter / OKR What company objective the work supports.
Priority 1 / 2 / 3 or Critical / Standard / Backlog.
Due date Real date; recurring tasks get recurrence.
Status Not started, In progress, Blocked, Done.
KPI / impact Revenue, funnel, operational or brand metric affected.
Dependency What must happen first or who is blocking it.
Notes / evidence Link to SOP, file, decision or result.
Recommended Roadmap views
 THIS WEEK - leadership commitments due before next Monday.
 QUARTERLY OKRs - objectives, KRs, score and linked projects.
 REVENUE PROJECTS - offer, funnel, campaigns, partnerships and pricing tests.
 CONTENT CALENDAR - HL Podcast, commercial batches, freestyle and event deliverables.
 EVENTS - event date, primary goal, owner, budget, checklist and scorecard.
 SOP LIBRARY - status of processes being documented.
 BLOCKED - every item waiting on a decision, person or dependency.
 DECISION LOG - important decisions such as Rockville, new hires, package changes or new room capacity.
Roadmap rule
If it is discussed Monday and needs action, it goes into the Roadmap before the meeting ends. If it is a lead, 
customer or sales follow-up, it stays in HighLevel.

title: Sop Library
body:
Document the work in the order revenue touches it
First 12 SOPs to build
Priority SOP Owner suggestion
1 New lead response + qualification Marketing/Sales
2 Podcast tour experience Jaco + Sales
3 Proposal + follow-up sequence Marketing/Sales
4 Recurring package close + autopay Jaco + Sales
5 Podcast client onboarding Podcast Producer / JoJo
6 Podcast room setup + preflight JoJo / Engineers
7 Session execution + client experience Engineers
8 File naming, backup + delivery handoff JoJo / Editors
9 Video edit + QA + revision Editing lead
10 Recurring client success + renewal Client Success
11 Monthly event playbook Leadership / Event owner
12 Monday / Wednesday / Sunday meeting 
process Jaco + JoJo
Simple SOP format
 Purpose - why this process exists.
 Trigger - what starts the process.
 Owner - one accountable role.
 Inputs - information/files needed.
 Steps - 5-12 clear actions with screenshots/links only where useful.
 Quality check - what must be true before completion.
 SLA - expected timing.
 Escalation - what happens when something goes wrong.
 Version / last updated - keep it living.
Do not spend weeks writing perfect manuals. Build the SOP while the task is being done, test it with an intern or 
engineer, then improve the confusing parts.

title: Capital Allocation + Risk
body:
Protect cash while the engine is still proving itself
Capital priorities
Priority Rule
1. Keep the lights on Maintain enough cash to cover fixed obligations and avoid growth 
decisions made from panic.
2. Measure margins Know direct cost and contribution margin by service before 
scaling ad spend or discounting packages.
3. Fund what converts Reinvest in campaigns, sales systems, editors and capacity only 
when the scoreboard shows a return.
4. Build a reserve Work toward 2-3 months of fixed operating expenses before 
major expansion.
5. Invest in pillars from profit Use podcast profits, not gross revenue, to fund larger 
Music/Media/Merch bets.
Major risks and mitigations
Risk How it shows up Mitigation
Founder concentration Jaco/JoJo become the routing layer for every 
decision
SOPs, role scorecards, Roadmap, triggered 
contractor hires.
Lead volume without sales discipline Many tours, few payments Same-day proposal, sales coaching, funnel 
KPIs and call/tour review.
Sales without retention First-sale revenue rises but MRR stays flat Recurring offer, client-success cadence, 
reserved slots and renewal process.
Post-production bottleneck Late edits and revision chaos Editor bench, templates, briefs, QA and 
capacity thresholds.
Too-broad ICP Ads generate low-budget or low-intent leads Qualifying language, persona-specific 
creative, lead scoring.
Creative distraction Events/merch/media consume leadership 
time without returns
Quarterly OKRs, 65% growth allocation and 
event scorecards.
Expansion too early Second room or major gear purchase drains 
cash
Utilization trigger and business case before 
capital spend.
Capital discipline
The company should feel underbuilt before it expands physical capacity. A busy calendar is not enough; prove 
sustained utilization, waitlist pressure, healthy margins and delivery capacity first.

20  /  90-DAY EXECUTION PLAN
The first 12 weeks
Week Primary objective Deliverable
1 Install the scoreboard
Baseline current revenue, MRR, lead sources, 
tours, show rate, close rate, room hours and 
turnaround. Roadmap updated.
2 Finalize offer ladder Cost-check recurring packages; create one-
page package sheet and tour close options.
3 Fix the tour-to-proposal flow
Tour checklist, discovery questions, same-
day proposal template and follow-up 
automation.
4 Launch recurring conversion Every first-session client receives a relevant 
recurring option; measure conversion.
5 Build ad creative system
Use first commercial batch to create multiple 
hooks/personas; track campaign-to-revenue 
attribution.
6 Build referral engine
Create referral ask, partner list and intro offer 
for agencies, professionals and existing 
clients.
7 Run event as acquisition Monthly event with QR/CRM capture, clear 
primary KPI and post-event tour offer.
8 Harden client success Kickoff brief, reserved slots, delivery 
checklist, testimonial/referral moment.
9 Coach sales with data
Review lost tours, objections and proposals; 
improve script/offer instead of just buying 
more leads.
10 Build the proof library
Organize testimonials, best clips, BTS, set 
photos and use cases by ICP for ads and 
tours.
11 Cost + capacity review Measure editor hours, margin, room 
utilization, revision rate and delivery backlog.
12 Quarter review + next OKRs Score KRs, keep/kill experiments, set next-
quarter targets and update Roadmap.
What should be true after 90 days
 HighLife knows exactly where every podcast lead is in the funnel.
 Tours have a repeatable discovery and closing flow.
 Recurring packages are being sold and retention is measured.
 Monday leadership decisions are based on one scoreboard.
 The Roadmap contains current OKRs, owners and due dates.
 At least the first 12 revenue-critical SOPs are drafted or actively being built.
 Content and events run on cadence without stealing the company from revenue execution.
 Leadership can say which channel, offer and client type creates the best economics.

title: Decision Rules
body:
The HighLife guardrails
Rule Meaning
1. Podcast is the cash engine through 2027 Unless data disproves the thesis, 60%-70% of growth energy 
goes here.
2. Three quarterly objectives maximum New ideas compete for backlog unless they directly support an 
OKR.
3. Every task gets one owner Shared ownership usually means no ownership.
4. No second room before capacity proof Use utilization and waitlist data, not excitement.
5. No large merch inventory without demand proof Use preorder/limited-drop tests.
6. Every event has a primary KPI Revenue, leads, content or community - know why it exists.
7. Sell recurring before discounting Increase account value through service depth and convenience.
8. Track profit drivers, not just revenue Direct labor, commission, ad spend and revision load determine 
what is worth scaling.
9. Protect the brand Premium price requires premium reliability, communication and 
final output.
10. Reinvest from strength Podcast profit should fund larger Music, Media and Merch bets 
after the core machine is healthy.
The weekly question
What is the single highest-leverage thing HighLife can do this week to increase durable revenue without 
damaging quality or the brand?

title: Appendix
body:
Source snapshot + founder whiteboard
Public HighLife facts used in this plan
 HighLife public site describes the company as a full-service recording studio, production team and creative community, and 
states that more than 1,000 creatives have used the business.
 HighLife story page states the company was founded in 2019, Jaco joined JoJo as a partner in 2021, and the company 
operates DC and Rockville locations with a broader engineering team.
 Public podcast page: video podcast production starts at $300/hour; audio starts at $100/hour; post-production pricing 
includes video editing, audio editing, mixing/mastering and short-form clips; on-location recording is also offered.
 Public recording page lists DC recording sessions at $75/hour and Rockville at $60-$70/hour, broadly consistent with the 
internal ~$70/hour music-studio reference used in this plan.
 Values referenced: Artist First, Fearless Creativity, Respect & Integrity, Adapt & Innovate.
Internal assumptions / management inputs
 Current average revenue: ~$9K/month, with ~$8K from the music studio and ~$1K from podcasting.
 Official cumulative target: $250K from Aug. 10, 2026 through Dec. 31, 2027.
 Music-studio current hourly model ceiling estimated by leadership at ~$10K-$12K/month.
 Podcast room: one room, 3-4 set configurations, one show at a time, with existing staff/equipment to operate it.
 New marketing/sales partner handles full-service marketing, ads, AI outbound, CRM/HighLevel and sales; 15% commission 
on the first sale.
 Leadership today is Jaco + JoJo; team includes engineers and interns.
 Target podcast customers are established professionals/brands with a clear business or media reason to publish and ability 
to pay premium production pricing.
External web source review date: August 10, 2026. This document is an internal management plan, not legal, tax 
or accounting advice. Package prices marked "recommended" are strategic drafts and should be finalized after 
labor and margin analysis.
